title: Speeds and feeds for 6061 aluminum vs 4140 steel on a manual lathe
summary: Side-by-side starting SFPM, RPM, and feed guidance for 6061 vs 4140 on a manual lathe — then how to adjust by chip and sound.

blocks.title: Same diameter, two metals, different SFPM
blocks.body: 6061 aluminum wants speed; 4140 steel wants respect. This page puts starting surface feet per minute, RPM, and feed side by side for a manual lathe, then shows how to tune from chips and sound — not from blind faith in a chart.

items.label: Surface feet per minute at the cut
Inches per revolution (IPR) on the carriage

columns.name: 6061-T6 aluminum
columns.detail: Fast SFPM, sharper tools, watch built-up edge. Coolant or mist helps finish; many hobby cuts run dry with air blast. Light DOC still cuts cleanly when the edge is keen.

columns.name: 4140 steel (annealed / prehard examples)
columns.detail: Lower SFPM, rigid setup, consistent feed. HSS works; carbide likes steady chipload. Prematurely hard grades need even more conservative starts. Never starve the cut with timid feed that rubs.

blocks.heading: Example starting SFPM (HSS / general-purpose carbide)
blocks.caption: Starting bands only. Tool geometry, stickout, machine HP, and whether 4140 is annealed vs prehard move these numbers a lot.

blocks.heading: Example RPM at Ø1.000 in (using RPM ≈ SFPM × 3.82)
rows: Many small lathes top out — gear down if noisy
May exceed hobby spindle limits; use what you have safely
blocks.caption: Halve RPM when you double diameter. Always respect your machine's rated speed and chuck rating.

blocks.heading: Example feed (IPR) starting points
blocks.caption: Undernourished feed that only rubs heats the edge — especially in steel.

blocks.heading: Tune from evidence, not ego
items: Start at the low-middle of the SFPM band for your tool and material.
Take a short trial cut. Read chip color/shape, surface, and sound.
Aluminum: stringy birds-nest or built-up edge → sharper tool, more speed/rake help, clear chips. Squeal → check stickout and speed.
Steel: blue chips on HSS may mean too fast; shiny rubbed surface with heat → increase feed slightly or fix sharpness; chatter → reduce stickout, change speed, or DOC.
Only then write your shop's personal numbers on the chart.

blocks.title: Manual lathe realities
blocks.body: Long aluminum chips wrap. Steel parting binds. Unbalanced chuck speeds are limited for a reason. These tables do not override your machine manual, tool maker data, or common sense about guards and eye protection.

blocks.heading: Quick check
blocks.prompt: You move from Ø1 in 6061 to Ø2 in 4140 on HSS roughing. What should happen to RPM first?
options: Double RPM because steel is tougher
Drop SFPM for steel and roughly half again for the larger diameter
Keep the same RPM and only change feed
blocks.explanation: 4140 wants much lower SFPM than 6061, and doubling diameter halves RPM for the same SFPM. Both effects cut speed hard.

blocks.heading: Shop next step
blocks.body: Print the SFPM table, pencil your lathe's real RPM limits beside it, and record one good cut in each metal this week.
